sentences.zh: ○苗晉卿裴冕裴遵慶子向向子寅寅子樞=苗晉卿=苗晉卿，上黨壺關人。

translations.literal: [Section:] Miao Jinqing, Pei Mian, Pei Zunqing, his son Xiang, Xiang's son Yin, Yin's son Shu. = Miao Jinqing = Miao Jinqing was a native of Huguan in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: This section covers Miao Jinqing, Pei Mian, and Pei Zunqing, together with Pei Xiang, Xiang's son Yin, and Yin's grandson Shu. Miao Jinqing was from Huguan in Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 世以儒素稱。

translations.literal: His family for generations was famed for Confucian simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: His lineage was known for upright Confucian learning and modest living.

sentences.zh: 祖夔，高道不仕，追贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kui, of lofty virtue and did not take office, was posthumously awarded Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kui, a man of exalted principle who never held office, was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 父殆庶，官至絳州龍門縣丞，早卒，以晉卿贈太子少保。

translations.literal: His father Dai-shu, reached office as Assistant Magistrate of Longmen County in Jiang Prefecture, died early; because of Jinqing he was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dai-shu rose only to assistant magistrate of Longmen in Jiang prefecture and died young; on account of Jinqing's eminence he was posthumously granted the title Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 晉卿幼好學，善屬文，進士擢第。

translations.literal: Jinqing from youth loved learning, excelled at literary composition, and was selected in the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing had loved study from childhood, wrote well, and passed the jinshi civil examination.

sentences.zh: 初授懷州修武縣尉，歷奉先縣尉，坐累貶徐州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Initially appointed magistrate's assistant of Xiuwu County in Huai Prefecture, served as magistrate's assistant of Fengxian County, and because of entanglement in a case was demoted to Registrar of Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was first made magistrate's assistant at Xiuwu in Huai, then served at Fengxian, but was demoted to registrar at Xu prefecture after being implicated in an affair.

sentences.zh: 秩滿隨調，判入高等，授萬年縣尉。

translations.literal: When his term ended he joined the regular transfer; his written evaluation was graded in the upper rank, and he was appointed magistrate's assistant of Wannian County.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of his term he entered the routine reassignment pool, scored in the top tier on his evaluation, and received appointment as assistant magistrate of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史，歷度支、兵、吏部三員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attending Censor and served successively as Vice Director in the ministries of Revenue, War, and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to attending censor and then held vice-director posts in the revenue, war, and personnel ministries in turn.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年，遷吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan, he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 23 (735), he was made a director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，與吏部郎中孫逖並拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, together with Sun Ti, Director in the Ministry of Personnel, he was jointly appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he and Sun Ti of the personnel ministry were both promoted to drafter in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，以本官權知吏部選事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, with his existing office he was temporarily put in charge of personnel selection matters.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 27 he was given his existing rank but charged with directing the ministry's selection examinations.

sentences.zh: 晉卿性謙柔，選人有訴訟索好官者，雖至數千言，或聲色甚厲者，晉卿必含容之，略無慍色。

translations.literal: Jinqing's nature was modest and gentle; when candidates lodged complaints or sued for good posts, even if to several thousand words, or their voice and bearing were very fierce, Jinqing always bore with them, without a trace of anger.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing was modest and even-tempered: when examinees petitioned or quarreled for better appointments, sometimes at great length or with angry outbursts, he always listened patiently and never showed annoyance.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，拜吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 29 he was made vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 前後典選五年，政既寬弛，胥吏多因緣為奸，賄賂大行。

translations.literal: Over five years before and after in charge of selection, because administration was already lax, clerks often took advantage to commit wrongdoing, and bribery flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the examinations for five years in all; his rule was lenient and slack, so clerks seized every opening for graft and bribes became rampant.

sentences.zh: 時天下承平，每年赴選常萬余人。

translations.literal: At the time the empire enjoyed peace, and those who came each year to selection often exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Peace reigned under heaven, and more than ten thousand candidates presented themselves each year.

sentences.zh: 李林甫為尚書，專任廟堂，銓事唯委晉卿及同列侍郎宋遙主之。

translations.literal: Li Linfu as Minister devoted himself solely to the court altar, and selection affairs were solely entrusted to Jinqing and his colleague Vice Minister Song Yao to preside.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu held the ministerial post but kept his grip on court power, leaving the actual running of selections to Jinqing and his fellow vice minister Song Yao alone.

sentences.zh: 選人既多，每年兼命他官有識者同考定書判，務求其實。

translations.literal: Because candidates were numerous, each year additional appointment was made of other officials with discernment to join in evaluating written judgments, striving to seek the real quality.
translations.idiomatic: With so many candidates, each year other capable officials were also assigned to grade the written examinations, so that the results might reflect real merit.

sentences.zh: 天寶二年春，御史中丞張倚男奭參選，晉卿與遙以倚初承恩，欲悅附之，考選人判等凡六十四人，分甲乙丙科，奭在其首。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Tianbao, Zhang Yi, Vice Censor-in-Chief, his son Shi participated in selection; Jinqing and Yao because Yi had newly received favor wished to please and attach to him—they evaluated candidates' written grades totaling sixty-four persons, dividing into First, Second, and Third classes, with Shi at their head.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Tianbao 2 (743), Zhang Yi's son Shi entered the examinations. Jinqing and Yao, eager to curry favor with the newly favored Zhang Yi, ranked sixty-four candidates in three tiers and placed Shi at the top.

sentences.zh: 眾知奭不讀書，論議紛然。

translations.literal: The crowd knew Shi did not read books, and discussion was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knew Shi was unlettered, and protest swirled through the capital.

sentences.zh: 有蘇孝慍者，嘗為范陽薊令，事安祿山，具其事告之。

translations.literal: There was one Su Xiaoyin, who had once been magistrate of Ji in Fanyang, served An Lushan, and reported the full matter to him.
translations.idiomatic: A former magistrate of Ji in Fanyang named Su Xiaoyin, now in An Lushan's service, reported the whole affair to him in detail.

sentences.zh: 祿山恩寵特異，謁見不常，因而奏之。

translations.literal: Lushan enjoyed exceptional grace and favor; audiences were not regular, and so through this he memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan enjoyed unusual imperial favor and did not often attend court, so he used this occasion to lay the matter before the throne.

sentences.zh: 玄宗大集登科人，禦花萼樓親試，登第者十無一二；

translations.literal: Xuanzong greatly gathered those who had passed the examinations, personally tested them at the Hua'e Pavilion; of those who had received degrees, not one or two in ten [passed].
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong convened all the newly accredited candidates and personally examined them at the Hua'e Tower; fewer than one or two in ten of those already listed as passed could meet the test.

sentences.zh: 而奭手持試紙，竟日不下一字，時謂之「曳白」。

translations.literal: But Shi, holding the examination paper, all day did not write a single character; they at the time called it "dragging the blank."
translations.idiomatic: Shi held his examination slip and wrote not a single character all day long, and contemporaries dubbed him "the dragged blank."

sentences.zh: 上怒，晉卿貶為安康郡太守，遙為武當郡太守，張倚為淮陽太守。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry; Jinqing was demoted to Prefect of Ankang commandery, Yao to Prefect of Wudang commandery, Zhang Yi to Prefect of Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's rage sent Jinqing to Ankang as prefect, Yao to Wudang, and Zhang Yi to Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「門庭之間，不能訓子；

translations.literal: Edict said: "Within one's gate and courtyard, unable to instruct his son;
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "In his own household he could not discipline his son;

sentences.zh: 選調之際，仍以托人。」

translations.literal: at the time of selection and appointment, still relied on entrusting it to others.
translations.idiomatic: and at the time of civil selection he still had to plead on his son's behalf.

sentences.zh: 時士子皆以為戲笑。

translations.literal: At the time scholars all took it as jest and ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars of the day repeated it as a bitter joke.

sentences.zh: 天寶三載閏二月，轉魏郡太守，充河北采訪處置使，居職三年，政化洽聞。

translations.literal: In the intercalary second month of the third year of Tianbao, he was transferred to Prefect of Wei commandery, serving as Hebei Investigating and Disposing Commissioner; in office three years, his government and transformation were harmoniously heard of.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary second month of Tianbao 3 he became prefect of Wei and Hebei investigating commissioner; after three years his administration was celebrated throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 會入計，因上表請歸鄉里。

translations.literal: When the occasion came to enter for the annual accounting, he therefore submitted a memorial requesting to return to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: When he traveled to court for the annual account, he memorialized asking leave to revisit his home.

sentences.zh: 既至壺關，望縣門而步。

translations.literal: Having reached Huguan, he viewed the county gate and walked on foot.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Huguan he dismounted and walked at the sight of the county gate.

sentences.zh: 小吏進曰：「太守位高德重，不宜自輕。」

translations.literal: A minor clerk advanced saying: "The prefect's position is high and his virtue heavy; it is not fitting to belittle oneself.
translations.idiomatic: A junior clerk protested: "Your rank and standing are too exalted to show such humility.

sentences.zh: 晉卿曰：「《禮》：『下公門，式路馬。』

translations.literal: Jinqing said: "The Rites: 'When descending from the duke's gate, one salutes the road horses.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing replied: "The Rites say: 'When you leave a nobleman's gate, you bow to the horses on the road.

sentences.zh: 況父母之邦，所宜尊敬。

translations.literal: How much more in the land of one's father and mother—what is fitting is reverence.
translations.idiomatic: How much more ought one to show reverence in the land of one's parents.

sentences.zh: 汝何言哉！」

translations.literal: What words are you speaking!"
translations.idiomatic: What nonsense is that!"

sentences.zh: 大會鄉黨，歡飲累日而去。

translations.literal: He greatly gathered the village and district, joyfully drank for successive days, and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: He gave a great feast for his kinsmen and neighbors and drank in celebration for days before leaving.

sentences.zh: 又俸錢三萬為鄉學本，以教授子弟。

translations.literal: Again he took thirty thousand in salary cash as capital for a village school, to instruct the sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He also endowed the local school with thirty thousand cash from his salary to teach the young men of the district.

sentences.zh: 尋改河東太守、河東采訪使，入為尚書、東京留守，征為憲部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Hedong Prefect and Hedong Investigating Commissioner, entered court as Minister and Eastern Capital Retention Officer, and was summoned as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made prefect and investigating commissioner of Hedong, then minister and eastern capital guardian in the capital, and finally summoned as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 屬祿山叛逆，楊國忠以晉卿有時望，將抑之，乃奏云：「宜以大臣鎮東道。」

translations.literal: At the time when Lushan rebelled, Yang Guozhong because Jinqing had contemporary reputation intended to suppress him and memorialized saying: "It is fitting to have a great minister guard the eastern way.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rose in rebellion, Yang Guozhong, wishing to curb Jinqing's standing at court, memorialized that a senior minister should be posted to guard the eastern route.

sentences.zh: 遂出為陜州刺史、陜虢兩州防禦使。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was sent out as Governor of Shaan Prefecture and Defense Commissioner of both Shaan and Guo prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore posted out as governor of Shaan and defense commissioner for Shaan and Guo.

sentences.zh: 及入對，固辭老病，由是忤旨，改憲部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: When he entered to respond, he firmly declined on grounds of old age and illness; by this he offended the imperial will and was changed to Minister of Justice retiring from office.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he pleaded old age and illness and thereby offended the emperor, who stripped him of active duty and let him retire as titular minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 及朝廷失守，衣冠流離道路，多為逆黨所脅，自陳希烈、張均已下數十人盡赴洛陽，晉卿潛遁山谷，南投金州。

translations.literal: When the court lost its hold, caps and gowns wandered the roads, many were compelled by the rebel party—from Chen Xilie, Zhang Jun, and below, several tens all went to Luoyang; Jinqing secretly fled through mountain valleys and south cast himself to Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, officials fled along the highways and many were forced into the rebels' ranks; dozens from Chen Xilie and Zhang Jun down went to Luoyang, but Jinqing hid in the hills and fled south to Jin prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會肅宗至鳳翔，手詔追晉卿赴行在，即日拜為左相，軍國大務悉以咨之。

translations.literal: When Suzong reached Fengxiang, by autograph edict he recalled Jinqing to the mobile court; that very day he was appointed Left Chancellor, and all great military and state affairs were entirely consulted with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong reached Fengxiang he sent a personal summons for Jinqing to join the mobile court and that same day named him left chancellor, consulting him on every major civil and military matter.

sentences.zh: 既收兩京，以功封韓國公，食實封五百戶，改為侍中。

translations.literal: Having recovered the two capitals, because of merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Han state, with substantive fief of five hundred households, and changed to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After the two capitals were retaken he was enfeoffed Duke of Han with five hundred taxable households and promoted to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 後以賊寇漸除，屢乞骸骨，優詔許之，罷知政事，為太子太傅。

translations.literal: Later because the bandit raiders were gradually eliminated, he repeatedly begged his old bones; a gracious edict permitted it, he ceased knowing administration, and became Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels waned he repeatedly asked to retire; the throne graciously agreed, relieved him of government, and made him grand tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝思舊臣，復拜為侍中。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor thought of old ministers and again appointed him Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor recalled his veteran counselor and again appointed him palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 晉卿寬厚廉謹，為政舉大綱，不問小過，所到有惠化。

translations.literal: Jinqing was generous, thick, honest, and cautious; in government he raised the great outline and did not inquire into small faults; wherever he arrived there was benevolent transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing was generous, upright, and discreet; in office he kept to broad principles and overlooked petty faults, and wherever he served he left a record of benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 魏人思之，為立碑頌德。

translations.literal: The people of Wei remembered him and erected a stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wei cherished his memory and raised a stele in praise of his virtue.

sentences.zh: 及秉鈞衡，小心畏慎，未嘗忤人意。

translations.literal: When he held the balance of state, he was careful and fearful in caution and never once went against people's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held the scales of power he was cautious and never gave offense.

sentences.zh: 性聰敏，達練事體，百司文簿，經目必曉，而修身守位，以智自全，議者比漢之胡廣。

translations.literal: His nature was clever and keen; he was thoroughly versed in the substance of affairs—documents of the hundred offices, once passed before his eyes he necessarily understood them; yet he cultivated himself and guarded his position, preserving himself by wisdom; commentators compared him to Hu Guang of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He was quick-witted and thoroughly versed in affairs; once he had glanced at any document from the ministries he understood it, yet he cultivated himself and guarded his post, preserving himself by tact; critics compared him to Hu Guang of the Han.

sentences.zh: 玄宗崩，肅宗詔晉卿攝冢宰。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong died, Suzong ordered Jinqing to act as regent.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong died, Suzong ordered Jinqing to serve as regent during the mourning.

sentences.zh: 上表固辭曰：「臣聞古者殷高宗在諒闇之中，百官聽於冢宰，更無事跡，但存文字。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial firmly declining, saying: "Your servant has heard that in antiquity, when King Gaozong of Yin was in the period of deep mourning, the hundred officials listened to the regent—there are no further traces of affairs, only written records remain.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized a firm refusal: "I have heard that in antiquity, when King Gaozong of Yin mourned in seclusion, the hundred officials obeyed the regent—but we have no further record of actual governance from that time, only words on paper.

sentences.zh: 且一時之事，禮不相沿。

translations.literal: Moreover, affairs of a single time—rites do not follow one another.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, that was a single occasion; ritual precedent does not bind every age.

sentences.zh: 今殘寇猶虞，日殷萬務，皆緣兵馬屯守討襲，善算良謀，立勝擒敵。

translations.literal: Now remnant bandits still give concern; daily the myriad affairs press in—all depend on armies garrisoned, guarding, attacking, and striking; good calculation and fine plans to achieve immediate victory and capture the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Today remnant rebels still threaten us and ten thousand affairs press in daily—all hinge on troops in the field, on sound strategy and swift victory over the enemy.

sentences.zh: 陛下若行古之道，居喪不言，蒼生何依，百事皆廢。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty follows the ancient way, dwelling in mourning and not speaking, on what will the black-haired people rely? A hundred affairs will all be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty followed the ancient way and held mourning silence, what would become of the people? Every affair of state would collapse.

sentences.zh: 伏讀國家起居註，亦於禮部檢見舊敕，恭惟太宗、高宗、、大行皇帝在位之日，皆有國哀，視事不輟，以為君臨天下，難徇常情。

translations.literal: Your servant has reverently read the national diary of activities and also in the Ministry of Rites examined old edicts; respectfully considering that in the days when Taizong, Gaozong, and the late emperor held the throne, whenever there was national mourning they did not cease attending to affairs, taking it that one who rules all under Heaven cannot follow ordinary sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: I have reverently read the court diary and old edicts in the Ministry of Rites: Taizong, Gaozong, and the late emperor, whenever the realm mourned, never ceased to govern, holding that a ruler of all under Heaven cannot indulge ordinary private feeling.

sentences.zh: 今遺詔有處分，皇帝宜三日而聽政。

translations.literal: Now the testamentary edict has provisions: the emperor ought on the third day to hear government.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's testament already directs that the new emperor should take up government after three days.

sentences.zh: 陛下遵太宗故事，則無冢宰；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty follows Taizong's precedent, then there is no regent;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty follows Taizong's precedent, no regent is needed;

sentences.zh: 遵大行皇帝遺詔，便合聽朝。

translations.literal: if you follow the late emperor's testamentary edict, then it is fitting at once to hear court.
translations.idiomatic: if you follow the late emperor's testament, you should take the throne at once.

sentences.zh: 萬姓颙颙，不勝大願。

translations.literal: The myriad people look up in hope—they cannot bear their great wish.
translations.idiomatic: The myriad people look up in hope with a longing that cannot be overstated.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下知理國之重，順人心之切，以義斷恩，從宜無改。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that Your Majesty knows the weight of governing the state, follows the urgency of people's hearts, cuts off private feeling by righteousness, and follows what is fitting without change.
translations.idiomatic: I trust Your Majesty knows how grave it is to govern the realm, how urgent the people's need is, and will set duty above private grief and do what the times require.

sentences.zh: 今朝臣一命已上，皆言臣心昏貌朽，加以疾病，事有急速，斷在須臾，凡聖不同，豈合受詔。

translations.literal: Now court ministers of the first rank and above all say that your servant's mind is dim and his appearance decayed, with illness added; affairs of urgency are decided in a moment; ordinary and sage are not the same—how could it be fitting to receive the edict?
translations.idiomatic: Every minister of the first rank and above says my mind is dim, my body worn, and my illness grave; urgent affairs are decided in an instant—a common man is no sage; how could I accept such a charge?

sentences.zh: 陛下發哀已五日矣，願準遺詔聽政，則四夷萬國，無任悲幸。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty has begun mourning for five days already; I wish you would follow the testamentary edict and hear government—then the four barbarians and ten thousand states will be unable to bear their grief and good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has mourned five days already; I pray you follow the testament and take up government—the four quarters and all nations will be overwhelmed with grief and relief alike.

sentences.zh: 肅宗時疾彌留，覽表殞絕，乃許。

translations.literal: Suzong at the time was gravely ill and near death; reading the memorial he collapsed as if dead, then permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong was then gravely ill; reading the memorial he fainted, then granted the request.

sentences.zh: 數日，肅宗晏駕，代宗踐祚，又詔晉卿攝冢宰。

translations.literal: Several days later Suzong died; Daizong ascended the throne and again ordered Jinqing to act as regent.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Suzong died and Daizong ascended the throne; he again ordered Jinqing to serve as regent.

sentences.zh: 晉卿上表懇辭曰：「臣以昔者天子居喪之時，百官聽於冢宰者，蓋君幼小，禦極事殷，情理當然。

translations.literal: Jinqing submitted a memorial earnestly declining, saying: "Your servant considers that in former times when the Son of Heaven dwelt in mourning and the hundred officials listened to the regent, it was because the ruler was young and small, the throne's affairs were pressing—reason and sentiment made it natural.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing memorialized again in earnest refusal: "In former times, when the Son of Heaven mourned and officials obeyed a regent, it was because the ruler was a child and the throne's burdens were overwhelming—that was only natural.

sentences.zh: 沿革不一，今古異同，而周武、漢文，合於通變，垂範作則，可舉而行。

translations.literal: Change and continuation are not uniform; present and ancient differ in sameness and difference—yet King Wu of Zhou and Emperor Wen of Han conformed to flexible adaptation, handed down models and made standards that may be raised up and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Custom has varied from age to age, yet King Wu of Zhou and Emperor Wen of Han adapted wisely to circumstance and left examples we may follow.

sentences.zh: 又士或墨缞，時遇金革，豈非銜恤，謂義在斷恩。

translations.literal: Again, a gentleman may wear black hemp mourning, yet when the time meets arms and armor, is it not that he harbors grief yet holds that righteousness lies in cutting off private feeling?
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman may wear mourning garb yet take up arms when the state is at war—he grieves inwardly but knows that duty must override private sorrow.

sentences.zh: 且百善之至，無加於孝也，其有容瘁心絕，指景悼生，此匹夫守節之常情，殊王者嗣續之大計。

translations.literal: Moreover, among the hundred virtues none surpasses filial piety; yet there are those whose countenance is haggard and heart broken, who point to the sun and mourn life—this is the ordinary sentiment of a common man keeping integrity, quite different from the great plan of a king's succession.
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety is the highest of virtues, yet to waste away in grief and mourn one's own life is the conduct of a private man—not the great duty of one who must carry on the royal line.

sentences.zh: 昨二十日，陛下於大行皇帝柩前即位，是承先帝遺顧之言，亦前代不易之典。

translations.literal: Yesterday, the twentieth day, Your Majesty at the bier of the late emperor ascended the throne—this carries out the late emperor's parting charge and is also an unchanging canon of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Only yesterday, on the twentieth, Your Majesty took the throne before the late emperor's bier—fulfilling his final charge and following an immemorial precedent.

sentences.zh: 則知所略不為害，所存是適權，防威滅端，所利者大。

translations.literal: Then one knows that what is set aside does no harm and what is preserved is fitting expedience—warding off peril and extinguishing the source; the benefit is great.
translations.idiomatic: What is set aside does no harm; what is preserved is timely expedience—cutting danger at the root brings the greater good.

sentences.zh: 陛下因心純至，天地明察。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's heart follows purity to the utmost; Heaven and Earth see clearly.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's heart is utterly sincere; Heaven and Earth discern it.

sentences.zh: 伏以報劬勞之恩，申罔極之思，終身之痛，豈計朝夕！

translations.literal: Your servant considers that repaying toilsome labor's grace and expressing boundless longing—lifelong pain, how could one reckon by days and nights!
translations.idiomatic: To repay a parent's toil and express boundless grief is a lifelong sorrow—not a matter of days alone!

sentences.zh: 但以一日之內，萬務在中，須達宸聰，始成國政。

translations.literal: Yet within a single day the myriad affairs lie at the center; the imperial ear must be reached before state government can be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within a single day ten thousand affairs press in; only when they reach Your Majesty's ear can the state be governed.

sentences.zh: 百僚萬姓及僧道耆壽等，相顧聚言，以臣老且無能，愚豈測聖，況久無居攝，臣不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: The hundred officials, myriad people, monks and Daoists, elders of long years, and others look at one another and gather in speech, saying your servant is old and without ability—how could stupidity measure sagehood? Moreover, for long there has been no regency; your servant dares not accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Officials, common people, monks, Daoists, and elders alike say I am old and incapable—how could a fool measure a sage? Regency has long been obsolete; I dare not accept the charge.

sentences.zh: 特乞陛下遵遺命，三日而政。

translations.literal: I specially beg Your Majesty to follow the testamentary command and govern after three days.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty only to follow the testament and take up government after three days.

sentences.zh: 臣博聽眾情，不勝懇願，伏望割痛抑哀，則天下悲幸。」

translations.literal: Your servant has broadly listened to the multitude's feelings and cannot bear the earnest wish; I bow and hope you will cut pain and restrain grief—then all under Heaven will be overwhelmed with grief and good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Having heard the people's voice, I cannot state their wish strongly enough: I pray you set aside private grief, and the realm will be overwhelmed with sorrow and relief together.

sentences.zh: 上號泣從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor wailed and wept and followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept aloud and assented.

sentences.zh: 時晉卿年已衰暮，又患兩足，上特許肩輿至中書，入閣不趨，累日一視事。

translations.literal: At the time Jinqing's years were already declining in old age and he also suffered in both feet; the Emperor specially permitted him to be carried in a litter to the Secretariat, to enter the pavilion without hurrying, and to attend to affairs once every several days.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing was then advanced in years and afflicted in both legs; the emperor specially allowed him a sedan chair to the Secretariat, exemption from hurrying into court, and attendance at affairs only every few days.

sentences.zh: 歷三朝，皆以謹密見稱。

translations.literal: Through three reigns he was in each case praised for caution and discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Through three reigns he was praised for caution and discretion.

sentences.zh: 廣德初，吐蕃寇長安。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangde, the Tibetans raided Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangde era the Tibetans attacked Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 晉卿時病臥於私第，蕃聞之，輿入逼脅，晉卿閉口不言，賊不敢害。

translations.literal: Jinqing at the time lay ill in his private residence; the Tibetans heard of it, entered by litter to coerce him, Jinqing closed his mouth and did not speak, and the bandits did not dare harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing lay ill at home; the Tibetans heard of him, came in a litter to coerce him, but he kept silent and they did not dare harm him.

sentences.zh: 及上自陜至，冊為太保，罷知政事，又詔以太保致仕。

translations.literal: When the Emperor came from Shaan, Jinqing was enfeoffed as Grand Guardian, ceased knowing administration, and was again ordered to retire as Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from Shaan, Jinqing was made grand guardian, relieved of government, and again ordered to retire with that title.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年四月薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yongtai he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of Yongtai 1 (765).

sentences.zh: 輟朝三日，令京兆少尹一員護喪事，緣葬諸物並官給，賻絹布五百段、米粟五百石。

translations.literal: Court was suspended three days; one Junior Administrator of the Capital was ordered to oversee funeral affairs; all items connected with burial were supplied by the state; condolence gifts were five hundred lengths of silk and cloth and five hundred piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourning lasted three days; a junior capital official was assigned to oversee the funeral; all burial expenses were paid by the state, with five hundred lengths of silk and cloth and five hundred piculs of grain as condolence gifts.

sentences.zh: 太常議謚曰「懿獻」。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices deliberated and gave the posthumous title "Yi-xian."
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices proposed the posthumous name Yi-xian ("Reverent and Dedicated").

sentences.zh: 初，晉卿東都留守，引用大理評事元載為推官。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jinqing was Eastern Capital Retention Officer, he brought in Yuan Zai, Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, as investigating officer.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Jinqing was eastern capital guardian, he had appointed Yuan Zai, an assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, as his investigating officer.

sentences.zh: 至是載為中書侍郎、平章事，懷舊恩，諷有司改謚曰文貞。

translations.literal: By this time Zai was Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-ordinating Minister; cherishing old grace, he hinted to the responsible offices to change the posthumous title to Wen-zhen.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yuan Zai was vice director of the Secretariat and chief minister; remembering old kindness, he prompted the authorities to change the posthumous name to Wen-zhen ("Cultured and Upright").

sentences.zh: 大歷七年，令配享肅宗廟庭。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dali, he was ordered to share sacrifice in Suzong's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 7 (772) he was ordered to share sacrifices in Suzong's temple.

sentences.zh: 裴冕，河東人也，為河東冠族。

translations.literal: Pei Mian was a man of Hedong and belonged to the foremost clan of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Mian was from Hedong and belonged to that region's leading clan.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，以門廕再遷渭南縣尉，以吏道聞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, through hereditary privilege he was twice promoted to magistrate's assistant of Weinan County and became known for the way of officials.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era he rose through hereditary privilege to magistrate's assistant of Weinan and won a reputation for administrative skill.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞王鉷充京畿采訪使，表為判官。

translations.literal: Wang Hong, Vice Censor-in-Chief, serving as Capital Region Investigating Commissioner, recommended him as judge.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong, vice censor-in-chief and capital-region investigating commissioner, recommended him as his judicial aide.

sentences.zh: 遷監察御史，歷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Investigating Censor and served successively as Palace Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to investigating censor and then served as palace attending censor.

sentences.zh: 冕雖無學術，守職通明，果於臨事，鉷甚委之。

translations.literal: Although Mian had no scholarly learning, in holding office he was clear and penetrating, decisive in facing affairs, and Hong greatly entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Mian lacked scholarly training, he was clear-minded in office and decisive in action, and Hong relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 及鉷得罪伏法，時宰臣李林甫方竊權柄，人鹹懼之，鉷賓佐數百，不敢窺鉷門。

translations.literal: When Hong was guilty and executed by law, at the time the chief minister Li Linfu was just usurping power; people all feared him; Hong's guest-officials numbered several hundred and did not dare peer at Hong's gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong was executed, Li Linfu held power and everyone feared him; Hong's hundreds of retainers dared not even approach his gate.

sentences.zh: 冕獨收鉷屍，親自護喪，瘞於近郊，冕自是知名。

translations.literal: Mian alone collected Hong's corpse, personally escorted the funeral, and buried him in the near suburbs; from this Mian became known.
translations.idiomatic: Mian alone recovered Hong's body, personally conducted the funeral, and buried him in the suburbs; from that day his name was known.

sentences.zh: 河西節度使哥舒翰表為行軍司馬，累遷員外郎中。

translations.literal: Geshu Han, Military Governor of Hexi, recommended him as campaigning marshal and he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han, military governor of Hexi, recommended him as campaigning marshal, and he rose through several vice-director posts.

sentences.zh: 玄宗幸蜀，至益昌郡，遙詔太子充天下兵馬元帥，以冕為御史中丞兼左庶子，為之副。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong went to Shu and reached Yichang commandery, from afar he issued an edict the Heir Apparent to serve as Commander-in-Chief of all armies and horses under Heaven, with Mian as Vice Censor-in-Chief and concurrent Left Subordinate of the Heir Apparent as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong fled to Shu and reached Yichang, he issued a distant edict making the heir apparent commander of all armies under heaven, with Mian as vice censor-in-chief and left subordinate of the heir as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 是時，冕為河西行軍司馬，授御史中丞，詔赴朝廷。

translations.literal: At this time Mian was campaigning marshal of Hexi; he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief and ordered by edict to proceed to court.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was then campaigning marshal in Hexi; he received appointment as vice censor-in-chief and was ordered to court.

sentences.zh: 遇太子於平涼，具陳事勢，勸之朔方，亟入靈武。

translations.literal: He met the Heir Apparent at Pingliang, fully stated the situation, urged him toward Shuofang, and urgently to enter Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: He met the heir apparent at Pingliang, laid out the situation in full, and urged him to go to Shuofang and enter Lingwu without delay.

sentences.zh: 冕與杜鴻漸、崔漪等勸進曰：「主上厭勤大位，南幸蜀川，宗社神器，須有所歸，天意人事，不可固違。

translations.literal: Mian together with Du Hongjian, Cui Yi, and others urged advancement, saying: "The sovereign has grown weary of the great position's toil and southward favors Shu; the altars of state and the sacred vessel must have someone to whom they return—Heaven's intent and human affairs cannot be stubbornly defied.
translations.idiomatic: Mian, Du Hongjian, Cui Yi, and others urged him to take the throne: "The sovereign has wearied of rule and gone south to Shu; the altars of state and the imperial regalia must find a home—Heaven's will and men's needs cannot be defied.

sentences.zh: 若逡巡退讓，失億兆心，則大事去矣！

translations.literal: If you hesitate and yield in retreat, losing the hearts of the myriad masses, then the great affair is lost!
translations.idiomatic: If you waver and stand aside, you will lose the hearts of countless people—and the throne will slip away forever.

sentences.zh: 臣等猶知之，況賢智乎！」

translations.literal: We your ministers still know this—how much more the wise and worthy!
translations.idiomatic: Even we know as much—how much more must the wise and talented among us!

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「南平寇逆，奉迎鑾輿，退居儲貳，侍膳左右，豈不樂哉！

translations.literal: The Crown Prince said: "To pacify the south and suppress rebels, welcome back the imperial carriage, withdraw to serve as heir, and attend meals at the sovereign's side—what could be more joyful!
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent said: "To pacify the south and crush the rebels, welcome back the imperial carriage, step back to serve as heir, and attend the sovereign at table—what could be happier than that!

sentences.zh: 公等何言之過也？」

translations.literal: Why do you gentlemen speak so extravagantly?"
translations.idiomatic: Why do you gentlemen go so far in what you say?"

sentences.zh: 冕與杜鴻漸又進曰：「殿下藉累聖之資，有天下之表。

translations.literal: Mian and Du Hongjian again advanced, saying: "Your Highness draws on the accumulated merit of successive sages and bears the outward bearing of one who holds all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Mian and Du Hongjian pressed again: "Your Highness inherits the accumulated virtue of successive sovereigns and carries the bearing of one destined to rule the realm.

sentences.zh: 元貞萬國，二十余年，殷憂啟聖，正在今日。

translations.literal: For more than twenty years primal rectitude has governed the myriad states; through grave anguish Heaven opens the way to sage rule—today is that day.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years the realm has endured deep trial; through that anguish Heaven has prepared a sage ruler—and today is the day.

sentences.zh: 所從殿下六軍將士，皆關輔百姓，日夜思歸。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers of the six armies following Your Highness are all common people of the Guanzhong region, day and night longing to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and soldiers of the six armies who follow you are all common folk from the Guanzhong heartland, longing day and night to go home.

sentences.zh: 大軍一散，不可復集，不如因而撫之以從眾，臣等敢以死請。」

translations.literal: Once the great army disperses it cannot be gathered again—better to take this occasion to console them and follow the multitude's will; we dare beg this at the cost of our lives."
translations.idiomatic: Once this great army scatters it cannot be reassembled—better to seize the moment, reassure the men, and follow their will; we beg this of you even at the cost of our lives."

sentences.zh: 凡勸進五上，乃依。

translations.literal: Altogether they urged advancement five times before he consented.
translations.idiomatic: They urged him to take the throne five times before he at last agreed.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，以定策功，遷中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，倚以為政。

translations.literal: When Suzong ascended the throne, for his merit in fixing the plan he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Secretariat and co-ordinating minister, and relied upon in governing.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong took the throne, Mian was promoted to vice minister of the Secretariat and co-ordinating minister for his role in settling the succession, and the emperor relied on him in governing.

sentences.zh: 冕性忠勤，悉心奉公，稍得人心。

translations.literal: Mian by nature was loyal and diligent, devoting himself wholeheartedly to public duty, and gradually won people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was loyal and industrious by nature, gave himself wholly to public service, and gradually won people's trust.

sentences.zh: 然不識大體，以聚人曰財，乃下令賣官鬻爵，度尼僧道士，以儲積為務。

translations.literal: Yet he did not grasp the larger pattern: holding that gathering people means wealth, he issued orders to sell offices and ranks, license Buddhist nuns, monks, and Daoist priests, making accumulation his sole aim.
translations.idiomatic: But he failed to see the larger picture. Taking the saying that gathering people is wealth as license to hoard revenue, he ordered the sale of offices and ranks and the licensing of nuns, monks, and Daoist priests, making stockpiling money his chief concern.

sentences.zh: 人不願者，科令就之，其價益賤，事轉為弊。

translations.literal: Those unwilling were compelled by statute to comply; prices kept falling lower, and the affair turned into a grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Those who did not wish to buy were forced by regulation to do so; prices sank ever lower, and the policy became a growing abuse.

sentences.zh: 肅宗移幸鳳翔，罷冕知政事，遷右僕射。

translations.literal: When Suzong moved his court to Fengxiang, Mian was removed from handling affairs of government and transferred to Right Vice Director of the Departments.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong moved the court to Fengxiang, Mian was removed from active governance and made right vice director of the departments.

sentences.zh: 兩京平，以功封冀國公，食實封五百戶。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were pacified, for his merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji with a stipend of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After the two capitals were recovered, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji with a stipend of five hundred households for his service.

sentences.zh: 尋加御史大夫、成都尹，充劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter he was additionally made Censor-in-Chief and Prefect of Chengdu, and appointed military governor of Jiannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made censor-in-chief and prefect of Chengdu, and appointed military governor of Jiannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 又入為右僕射。

translations.literal: He again entered the capital as Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned to the capital as right vice director.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，與裴遵慶等並集賢待制。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, he and Pei Zunqing and others were all made scholars awaiting edicts at the Jixian Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai he and Pei Zunqing and others were all appointed scholars awaiting edicts at the Jixian Academy.

sentences.zh: 代宗求舊，拜冕兼御史大夫，充護山陵使。

translations.literal: Daizong sought out veterans of former service and appointed Mian concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Commissioner for Guarding the Imperial Tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong looked to men of long service and appointed Mian concurrently censor-in-chief and commissioner for guarding the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 冕以幸臣李輔國權盛，將附之，乃表輔國親昵術士中書舍人劉烜充山陵使判官。

translations.literal: Mian, because favored minister Li Fuguo's power was great and intending to attach himself to him, submitted a memorial that Fuguo's close associate, the diviner and Drafting Secretary Liu Xuan, serve as aide to the tomb-guard commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Because the favored minister Li Fuguo's power was great and Mian meant to attach himself to him, he memorialized that Fuguo's close associate, the diviner and drafting secretary Liu Xuan, serve as aide to the tomb-guard commissioner.

sentences.zh: 烜坐法，冕坐貶施州刺史。

translations.literal: Liu Xuan was punished by law; Mian was demoted to Prefect of Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan was punished for breaking the law, and Mian was demoted to prefect of Shi.

sentences.zh: 數月，移澧州刺史，復征為左僕射。

translations.literal: Several months later he was transferred to Prefect of Li, then recalled again as Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was transferred to prefect of Li, then recalled to serve again as left vice director.

sentences.zh: 元載秉政。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai held the reins of government.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai held the reins of government.

sentences.zh: 載為新平縣尉，王鉷辟在巡內，冕常引之，載頗德冕。

translations.literal: Zai had been magistrate of Xinping County; Wang Hong recruited him within his inspection circuit, and Mian often recommended him—Zai owed Mian a considerable debt of gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Zai had once been magistrate of Xinping County; Wang Hong recruited him within his inspection circuit, and Mian often recommended him—Zai felt deep gratitude toward Mian.

sentences.zh: 會宰臣杜鴻漸卒，載遂舉冕代之。

translations.literal: When chief minister Du Hongjian died, Zai thereupon recommended Mian to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When chief minister Du Hongjian died, Zai recommended Mian to replace him.

sentences.zh: 冕時已衰瘵，載以其順己，引為同列。

translations.literal: Mian was by then feeble with chronic illness; Zai, because he yielded to him, brought him in as a fellow minister.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was by then broken with chronic illness; Zai, finding him compliant, brought him in as a fellow minister.

sentences.zh: 受命之際，蹈舞絕倒，載趨而扶起，代為謝詞。

translations.literal: At the moment of accepting appointment he danced in obeisance and collapsed; Zai hurried forward to lift him and spoke the words of thanks in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: At the moment of accepting the appointment he danced in obeisance and collapsed; Zai rushed forward to help him up and delivered the words of thanks in his place.

sentences.zh: 冕兼掌兵權留守之任，俸錢每月二千余貫。

translations.literal: Mian concurrently held military command and the duties of capital guardian; his salary exceeded two thousand strings of cash per month.
translations.idiomatic: Mian concurrently held military command and the duties of capital guardian, with a monthly salary of more than two thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 性本侈靡，好尚車服及營珍饌，名馬在櫪，直數百金者常十數。

translations.literal: By nature he was extravagant, fond of fine carriages and dress and of preparing rare delicacies; in his stable were a dozen or so famed horses worth several hundred gold pieces each.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was extravagant, fond of fine carriages and dress and of preparing rare delicacies; in his stable were a dozen or so famed horses worth several hundred gold pieces apiece.

sentences.zh: 每會賓友，滋味品數，坐客有昧於名者。

translations.literal: Whenever he entertained guests, the dishes were so many in variety and number that seated guests would not recognize some by name.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he entertained guests, the dishes were so many in variety and number that some seated guests could not even name what they were eating.

sentences.zh: 自創巾子，其狀新奇，市肆因而效之，呼為「僕射樣」。

translations.literal: He devised his own headcloth, novel in form; shops accordingly copied it, calling it the "Vice Director style."
translations.idiomatic: He designed his own headcloth, novel in shape; shops copied it and called it the "Vice Director style."

sentences.zh: 初代鴻漸，小吏以俸錢文簿白之，冕顧子弟，喜見於色，其嗜利若此。

translations.literal: When he first replaced Hongjian, a petty clerk reported on the salary ledger; Mian glanced at his sons and nephews, delight plain on his face—such was his greed for profit.
translations.idiomatic: When he first replaced Hongjian, a petty clerk reported on the salary ledger; Mian looked at his sons and nephews, delight plain on his face—such was his appetite for profit.

sentences.zh: 拜職未盈月，卒，大歷四年十二月也。

translations.literal: Less than a full month after taking the post he died—in the twelfth month of the fourth year of Dali.
translations.idiomatic: Less than a full month after taking office he died, in the twelfth month of the fourth year of Dali.

sentences.zh: 上悼之，輟朝三日，贈太尉，賻制五百匹、粟五百石。

translations.literal: The sovereign mourned him, halted court for three days, posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Mentor, and granted funeral silks of five hundred bolts and five hundred shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him, halted court for three days, posthumously enfeoffed him as grand mentor, and granted five hundred bolts of funeral silk and five hundred shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 裴遵慶，絳州聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Zunqing was a native of Wenxi in Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zunqing was from Wenxi in Jiang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 代襲冠冕，為河東著族。

translations.literal: For generations they inherited high rank and were a prominent clan of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they inherited high office and were a distinguished clan of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 遵慶志氣深厚，機鑒敏達，自幼強學，博涉載籍，謹身晦跡，不幹當世之務。

translations.literal: Zunqing's character was deep and his spirit substantial; keen in insight and quick in discernment, from youth he applied himself forcefully to study, broadly traversing the canonical records, keeping himself restrained and his traces hidden, never meddling in the affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing had a deep and steady temperament and was quick and perceptive in judgment. From youth he applied himself rigorously to study and read widely in the classics, keeping his conduct restrained and his name obscure, and never meddling in the affairs of the day.

sentences.zh: 以門廕累授潞府司法參軍，時年已老，未為人所知。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he was repeatedly appointed judicial aide in Lu Prefecture; by then he was already old and unknown to others.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he was repeatedly appointed judicial aide in Lu prefecture; by then he was already old and still unknown to the world.

sentences.zh: 隨調吏部，授大理寺丞，剖斷刑獄，舉正綱條，理行始著。

translations.literal: Following regular transfer to the Ministry of Personnel, he was appointed aide in the Court of Judicial Review; in adjudicating criminal cases and upholding statutory lines, his conduct in office first became evident.
translations.idiomatic: On regular transfer to the Ministry of Personnel he was appointed aide in the Court of Judicial Review; in adjudicating criminal cases and upholding the law, his administrative merit first became evident.

sentences.zh: 遷司門員外、吏部員外郎，專判南曹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Gate Office and Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, exclusively adjudicating the southern bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Gate Office and vice director in the Ministry of Personnel, with exclusive charge of the southern bureau.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，海內無事，九流輻輳會府，每歲吏部選人，動盈萬數。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era the empire was untroubled; the nine ranks of officeholders thronged the capital, and each year the Ministry of Personnel's candidates for selection often exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era the empire was at peace; men of every rank thronged the capital, and each year the Ministry of Personnel's candidates for office often exceeded ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 遵慶敏識強記，精核文簿，詳而不滯，時稱吏事第一，由是大知名。

translations.literal: Zunqing was keen in recognition and strong in memory, rigorously checking documents and ledgers—thorough yet unsluggish; of the time he was called first in personnel affairs, and from this his fame became great.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing was quick of mind and strong of memory, rigorously checking documents and ledgers—thorough yet never sluggish. Of the time he was called first in personnel affairs, and from this his fame became great.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，楊國忠當國，出不附己者例為外官，遵慶亦出為郡守。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao, when Yang Guozhong held power, those who did not attach themselves to him were routinely sent to outer posts; Zunqing too was sent out as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao, when Yang Guozhong held power, those who did not support him were routinely sent to provincial posts; Zunqing too was sent out as prefect.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，征拜給事中、尚書右丞、吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Suzong ascended the throne, Zunqing was summoned and appointed Drafting Secretary, Right Assistant in the Secretariat, and Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong took the throne, Zunqing was summoned and appointed drafting secretary, right assistant in the Secretariat, and vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 恭儉克己，遲重謹密，頗有時望。

translations.literal: Humble, frugal, and self-restrained, deliberate, weighty, careful and discreet, he enjoyed considerable standing among his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Humble, frugal, and self-restrained, deliberate and careful in manner, he enjoyed considerable standing among his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 上元中，蕭華輔政，素知遵慶，每奏見，累稱之，遷黃門侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era, Xiao Hua assisted in government, having long known Zunqing; whenever he had audience he repeatedly praised him, and Zunqing was promoted to Vice Minister of the Chancellery and co-ordinating minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shangyuan era Xiao Hua assisted in government and had long known Zunqing; whenever he had audience he repeatedly praised him, and Zunqing was promoted to vice minister of the Chancellery and co-ordinating minister.

sentences.zh: 廣德初，仆固懷恩阻兵汾上，指中官為詞，上以遵慶忠純，特遣往汾州宣慰懷恩。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangde, Pugu Huai'en held troops at bay on the Fen; citing the eunuchs as his grievance, the sovereign, knowing Zunqing's loyalty and integrity, specially dispatched him to Fenzhou to proclaim consolation to Huai'en.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Guangde, Pugu Huai'en held his army on the Fen River and cited the eunuchs as his grievance; the emperor, knowing Zunqing's loyalty and integrity, specially dispatched him to Fenzhou to proclaim consolation to Huai'en.

sentences.zh: 遵慶既見懷恩，具陳朝旨，懷恩引過聽命，將隨遵慶朝謁，為副將範誌誠以邪說惑之，懷恩遂以懼死為詞。

translations.literal: When Zunqing had met Huai'en, he fully set forth the court's intent; Huai'en admitted fault and awaited orders, intending to follow Zunqing to audience at court—but Vice General Fan Zhicheng deluded him with perverse talk, and Huai'en then pleaded fear of death.
translations.idiomatic: When Zunqing met Huai'en, he fully set forth the court's intent; Huai'en admitted fault and awaited orders and was about to follow Zunqing to audience at court—but vice general Fan Zhicheng deluded him with perverse talk, and Huai'en then pleaded fear of death.

sentences.zh: 會蕃寇陷京師，乘輿幸陜，遵慶自汾州奔赴行在。

translations.literal: Just then barbarian raiders captured the capital; the imperial carriage proceeded to Shanzhou, and Zunqing raced from Fenzhou to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: Just then barbarian raiders captured the capital; the imperial carriage proceeded to Shanzhou, and Zunqing raced from Fenzhou to the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 及乘輿還京，以遵慶為太子少傅。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, Zunqing was made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, Zunqing was made junior tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，與裴冕等並於集賢院待制，罷知政事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, together with Pei Mian and others he was made a scholar awaiting edicts at the Jixian Academy, and removed from handling affairs of government.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai, together with Pei Mian and others he was made a scholar awaiting edicts at the Jixian Academy and removed from active governance.

sentences.zh: 尋改吏部尚書、右僕射，復知選事。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Minister of Personnel and Right Vice Director, again handling selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made minister of personnel and right vice director, again handling selection affairs.

sentences.zh: 時選人天興縣尉陳琯於銓庭言詞不遜，淩突無禮，代宗詔付遵慶於省門鞭三十，貶為吉州員外司戶參軍。

translations.literal: At that time the candidate Chen Guan, magistrate of Tianxing County, was insolent in speech at the selection hall, overbearing and without courtesy; Daizong issued an edict that Zunqing have him flogged thirty strokes at the ministry gate and demoted to supplemental aide for household affairs in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the candidate Chen Guan, magistrate of Tianxing County, was insolent in speech at the selection hall, overbearing and without courtesy; Daizong ordered Zunqing to have him flogged thirty strokes at the ministry gate and demoted him to supplemental aide for household affairs in Ji prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遵慶敦守儒行，老而彌謹。

translations.literal: Zunqing staunchly upheld Confucian conduct, growing more careful in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing staunchly upheld Confucian conduct and grew more careful in old age.

sentences.zh: 嘗為風狂族侄撾登聞鼓告以不順，上知遵度，不省，其見信如此。

translations.literal: Once a deranged clansman's nephew beat the Drum of Direct Appeal accusing him of disloyalty; the sovereign knew Zunqing and paid no heed—such was the trust he enjoyed.
translations.idiomatic: Once a deranged clansman's nephew beat the Drum of Direct Appeal accusing him of disloyalty; the emperor knew Zunqing and paid no heed—such was the trust he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 大歷十年十月薨於位，年九十余。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the tenth year of Dali he died in office at over ninety.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the tenth year of Dali he died in office at over ninety.

sentences.zh: 遵慶初登省郎，嘗著《王政記》，述今古禮體，識者覽之，知有公輔之量。

translations.literal: When Zunqing first rose to a provincial bureau officer, he once authored Record of Royal Government, setting forth ancient and modern ritual forms; readers who saw it knew he had the capacity of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Zunqing first rose to a provincial bureau officer, he authored Record of Royal Government, setting forth ancient and modern ritual forms; readers who saw it knew he had the capacity of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 遵慶子 向子向，字傃仁，少以門廕歷官至太子司議郎。

translations.literal: Zunqing's son Xiang—Pei Xiang, styled Suren—through hereditary privilege in youth rose through offices to Secretary for Discussion of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing's son Xiang—Pei Xiang, styled Suren—through hereditary privilege in youth rose through offices to secretary for discussion of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 建中初，李紓為同州刺史，奏向為從事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, Li Shu was prefect of Tong Prefecture and recommended Xiang as his aide.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianzhong, Li Shu was prefect of Tong prefecture and recommended Xiang as his aide.

sentences.zh: 硃泚反，李懷光又叛河中，使其將趙貴先築壘於同州，紓來奔奉天，向領州務。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci rebelled; Li Huai'guang also rebelled in Hezhong, sending his general Zhao Guixian to build fortifications at Tong Prefecture; Shu fled to Fengtian, and Xiang took charge of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci rebelled; Li Huai'guang also rebelled in Hezhong, sending his general Zhao Guixian to build fortifications at Tong prefecture; Li Shu fled to Fengtian, and Xiang took charge of prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 貴先因脅縣尉林寶役徒板築，不及期，將斬之，吏人百姓奔竄。

translations.literal: Guixian forced the county magistrate Lin Bao to press conscript laborers into rammed-earth construction; when the deadline was not met he was about to execute Lin, and officials and common people fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Guixian forced the county magistrate Lin Bao to press conscript laborers into rammed-earth construction; when the deadline was not met he was about to execute Lin, and officials and common people fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 向即詣貴先軍壘，以逆順之理責之，貴先感悟，遂來降，故同州不陷。

translations.literal: Xiang immediately went to Guixian's camp and rebuked him on the principles of loyalty and rebellion; Guixian came to his senses and submitted, and so Tong Prefecture did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang immediately went to Guixian's camp and rebuked him on the principles of loyalty and rebellion; Guixian came to his senses and submitted, and so Tong prefecture did not fall.

sentences.zh: 向由是知名。

translations.literal: From this Xiang became known.
translations.idiomatic: From this Xiang became known.

sentences.zh: 累為京兆府戶曹，轉櫟陽、渭南縣令，奏課皆第一，朝廷亟聞其理行，擢為戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: He served successively as clerical officer in the metropolitan prefecture, then magistrate of Liyang and Weinan—his merit reports were always rated first; the court quickly heard of his governance and promoted him to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as clerical officer in the metropolitan prefecture, then magistrate of Liyang and Weinan—his merit reports were always rated first; the court quickly heard of his governance and promoted him to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 德宗季年，天下方鎮副倅多自選於朝，防一日有變，遂就而授之節制。

translations.literal: In the late years of Dezong, many deputy officers of frontier military commissioners were chosen from the capital in advance, so that if trouble arose on a given day they could be sent at once and granted full command.
translations.idiomatic: In the late years of Dezong, many deputy officers of frontier military commissioners were chosen from the capital in advance, so that if trouble arose on a given day they could be sent at once and granted full command.

sentences.zh: 向已選為太原少尹，德宗召見喻旨，尋用為行軍司馬、兼御史中丞，改汾州刺史，轉鄭州。

translations.literal: Xiang had already been selected as vice prefect of Taiyuan; Dezong summoned him, explained his intent, and soon employed him as campaigning marshal and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, then changed him to Prefect of Fen and transferred him to Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang had already been selected as vice prefect of Taiyuan; Dezong summoned him, explained his intent, and soon employed him as campaigning marshal and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, then changed him to prefect of Fen and transferred him to Zheng.

sentences.zh: 又復為太原少尹，兼河東節度副使。

translations.literal: He again became vice prefect of Taiyuan and concurrent deputy military governor of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He again became vice prefect of Taiyuan and concurrent deputy military governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 改晉州刺史，充本州防禦使，遷虢州刺史。

translations.literal: He was changed to Prefect of Jin, serving as defense commissioner of that prefecture, then transferred to Prefect of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to prefect of Jin, serving as defense commissioner of that prefecture, then transferred to prefect of Guo.

sentences.zh: 入為京兆少尹，拜同州刺史，充本州防禦使。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as vice prefect of the metropolitan prefecture, was appointed Prefect of Tong, and served as defense commissioner of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as vice prefect of the metropolitan prefecture, was appointed prefect of Tong, and served as defense commissioner of that prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入為大理寺卿，出遷陜虢都防禦、觀察使。

translations.literal: He entered as Director of the Court of Judicial Review and was transferred out as defense and observation commissioner of the Shan-Guo region.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as director of the Court of Judicial Review and was transferred out as defense and observation commissioner of the Shan-Guo region.

sentences.zh: 三歲，拜左散騎常侍，自常侍復為大理。

translations.literal: After three years he was appointed Left Regular Attendant; from regular attendant he returned again to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was appointed left regular attendant; from regular attendant he returned again to the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 向本以名相子，以學行自飭，謹守其門風。

translations.literal: Xiang was originally the son of a famed chief minister; he disciplined himself through learning and conduct, carefully preserving his family's tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was originally the son of a famed chief minister; he disciplined himself through learning and conduct and carefully preserved his family's tradition.

sentences.zh: 歷官仁智推愛，利及於人。

translations.literal: In every post he showed benevolence and wisdom, extending care so that others benefited.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he showed benevolence and wisdom, extending care so that others benefited.

sentences.zh: 至是，以年過致政，朝廷優異，乃以吏部尚書致仕於新昌裏第。

translations.literal: By then, having passed the age for retirement, the court treated him with special favor and allowed him to retire as Minister of Personnel from his mansion in Xinchang Lane.
translations.idiomatic: By then, having passed the age for retirement, the court treated him with special favor and allowed him to retire as minister of personnel from his mansion in Xinchang Lane.

sentences.zh: 內外支屬百余人，向所得俸祿，必同其費，及領外任，亦挈而隨之。

translations.literal: More than a hundred kin inside and outside the clan—whatever salary Xiang received, he always shared the expenses equally; when he held outside posts he took them along as well.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred kin inside and outside the clan—whatever salary Xiang received, he always shared the expenses equally; when he held outside posts he took them along as well.

sentences.zh: 有孤煢疾苦不能自恤，向尤周給，至今稱其孝睦焉。

translations.literal: For those orphaned, alone, ill, or suffering who could not care for themselves, Xiang especially provided in full measure; to this day his filial piety and harmony are praised.
translations.idiomatic: For those orphaned, alone, ill, or suffering who could not care for themselves, Xiang especially provided in full measure; to this day his filial piety and harmony are praised.

sentences.zh: 大和四年九月卒，年八十。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Dahe he died at age eighty.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Dahe he died at age eighty.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as junior mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 向子 寅子寅，登進士第，累官至御史大夫卒。

translations.literal: Xiang's son Yin—Pei Yin—passed the jinshi examination and rose through offices to Censor-in-Chief, at which rank he died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's son Yin—Pei Yin—passed the jinshi examination and rose through offices to censor-in-chief, at which rank he died.

sentences.zh: 寅子 樞子樞，字紀聖，咸通十二年登進士第。

translations.literal: Yin's son Shu—Pei Shu, styled Jisheng—passed the jinshi examination in the twelfth year of Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's son Shu—Pei Shu, styled Jisheng—passed the jinshi examination in the twelfth year of Xiantong.

sentences.zh: 宰相杜審權出鎮河中，辟為從事，得秘書省校書郎，再遷藍田尉。

translations.literal: When chief minister Du Shenquan went out to command Hezhong, he recruited Shu as aide; Shu received appointment as proofreader in the Secretariat and was twice promoted to magistrate of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: When chief minister Du Shenquan went out to command Hezhong, he recruited Shu as aide; Shu received appointment as proofreader in the Secretariat and was twice promoted to magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 直弘文館。

translations.literal: He served on duty at the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He served on duty at the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 大學士王鐸深知之，鐸罷相失職，樞亦久之不調。

translations.literal: Grand Academician Wang Duo thought highly of him; when Duo lost his chancellorship and his position, Shu also went long without reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Academician Wang Duo thought highly of him; when Duo lost his chancellorship and his position, Shu also went long without reassignment.

sentences.zh: 從僖宗幸蜀，中丞李煥奏為殿中侍御史，遷起居郎。

translations.literal: Following Xizong to Shu, Vice Censor Li Huan recommended him as Palace Attendant Censor; he was promoted to Court Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: Following Xizong to Shu, vice censor Li Huan recommended him as palace attendant censor; he was promoted to court diarist.

sentences.zh: 中和初，王鐸復見用，以舊恩徙為鄭滑掌書記、檢校司封郎中，賜金紫，入朝歷兵、吏二員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhonghe, Wang Duo was again employed; out of old kindness Shu was transferred to chief secretary of Zheng-Hua and acting Director of the Department of Feudal Ranks, granted gold seal and purple robe; entering court he served successively as vice director in the Ministries of War and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhonghe, Wang Duo was again employed; out of old kindness Shu was transferred to chief secretary of Zheng-Hua and acting director of the Department of Feudal Ranks, granted gold seal and purple robe; entering court he served successively as vice director in the ministries of War and Personnel.

sentences.zh: 龍紀初，擢拜給事中，改京兆尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longji he was promoted to Drafting Secretary and changed to Prefect of the Metropolitan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longji he was promoted to drafting secretary and changed to prefect of the metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宰相孔緯尤深獎遇。

translations.literal: Chief minister Kong Wei especially favored and promoted him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Kong Wei especially favored and promoted him.

sentences.zh: 大順中，緯以用兵無功貶官，樞坐累為右庶子，尋出為歙州刺史。

translations.literal: In Dazhun, Wei was demoted for military failure without achievement; Shu was implicated and made Right Subordinate of the Heir Apparent, soon sent out as Prefect of She.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhun, Wei was demoted for military failure without achievement; Shu was implicated and made right subordinate of the heir apparent, soon sent out as prefect of She.

sentences.zh: 乾寧初，入為右散騎常侍，從昭宗幸華州，為汴州宣諭使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianning he entered as Right Regular Attendant; following Zhaozong to Huazhou he served as envoy to proclaim the edicts at Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qianning he entered as right regular attendant; following Zhaozong to Huazhou he served as envoy to proclaim the edicts at Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，樞自歙州罷郡歸朝，路經大梁，時硃全忠兵威已振，樞以兄事之，全忠由是重之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.

sentences.zh: 及樞傳詔，全忠皆稟朝旨，獻奉相繼，昭宗甚悅，遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 時崔胤專政，亦倚全忠，二人因是相結，改樞吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 未幾，換戶部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he was switched to Vice Minister of Revenue and co-ordinating minister.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was switched to vice minister of revenue and co-ordinating minister.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，昭宗幸華州，崔胤貶官，樞亦為工部尚書。

translations.literal: That winter Zhaozong went to Huazhou; Yin was demoted and Shu was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zhaozong went to Huazhou; Yin was demoted and Shu was made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 天子自岐下還宮，以樞檢校右僕射、同平章事，出為廣南節度使。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven returned to the palace from below Qi, Shu was made Acting Right Vice Director and co-ordinating minister and sent out as military governor of Guangnan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven returned to the palace from below Qi, Shu was made acting right vice director and co-ordinating minister and sent out as military governor of Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 制出，硃全忠保薦之，言樞有經世才，不可棄之嶺表，尋復拜門下侍郎，監修國史，累兼吏部尚書，判度支。

translations.literal: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as Minister of Personnel, administering the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed vice minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as minister of personnel, administering the treasury.

sentences.zh: 崔胤誅，以全忠素厚，相位如故。

translations.literal: When Cui Yin was executed, because of his longstanding closeness to Quanzhong Shu's chancellorship remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: After Cui Yin's execution, Shu's ties to Quanzhong kept him in the chancellorship unchanged.

sentences.zh: 從昭宗遷洛陽，駐蹕陜州，進右僕射、弘文館大學士、太清宮使，充諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: Following Zhaozong's move to Luoyang, when the court halted at Shanzhou, Shu was promoted to Right Vice Director, Grand Academician of the Hongwen Academy, Commissioner of the Palace of Great Clarity, and Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport across all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Following Zhaozong's move to Luoyang, when the court halted at Shanzhou, Shu was promoted to right vice director, grand academician of the Hongwen Academy, commissioner of the Palace of Great Clarity, and commissioner for salt and iron transport across all circuits.

sentences.zh: 哀帝初嗣位，柳璨用事，全忠嘗奏用牙將張廷範為太常卿，諸相議，樞曰：「廷範勛臣，幸有方鎮節鉞之命，何藉樂卿？

translations.literal: When Emperor Aidi first succeeded to the throne, Liu Can held power; Quanzhong once memorialized that his guard general Zhang Tingfan be made Minister of Ceremonies—the chancellors deliberated, and Shu said: "Tingfan is a meritorious minister; it would be fitting to grant him a frontier command with military insignia—why need he the post of Master of Music?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aidi first succeeded to the throne, Liu Can held power; Quanzhong once memorialized that his guard general Zhang Tingfan be made minister of ceremonies—the chancellors deliberated, and Shu said: "Tingfan is a meritorious minister; it would be fitting to grant him a frontier command with military insignia—why need he the post of master of music?

sentences.zh: 恐非元帥梁王之旨。」

translations.literal: I fear this is not the intent of Marshal, King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: I fear this is not the intent of Marshal, King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 乃持之不下。

translations.literal: He therefore held it and would not issue it.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore withheld the appointment and would not issue it.

sentences.zh: 俄而全忠聞樞言，謂賓佐曰：「吾常以裴十四器識真純，不入浮薄之伍，觀此議論，本態露矣。」

translations.literal: Before long Quanzhong heard Shu's words and said to his guest-officials: "I have always considered Pei the Fourteenth's capacity and insight truly pure, not entering the ranks of the frivolous and shallow—viewing this discussion, his true nature is revealed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Quanzhong heard what Shu had said and told his staff: "I always thought Pei the Fourteenth was genuinely upright and above the shallow crowd—but this remark shows his true colors.

sentences.zh: 切齒含怒。

translations.literal: He ground his teeth and harbored anger.
translations.idiomatic: He ground his teeth in fury.

sentences.zh: 柳璨聞全忠言，尋希旨罷樞相位，和陵祔享，拜尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Liu Can heard Quanzhong's words and soon, to please his intent, removed Shu from the chancellorship; at the joint offering at He-ling, Shu was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can heard Quanzhong's words and soon, to please him, stripped Shu of the chancellorship; at the joint offering at He-ling, Shu was made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 五月，責授朝散大夫、登州刺史，尋再貶瀧州司戶。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was punished and appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Governor of Deng Prefecture; soon he was again demoted to Registrar of Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was demoted to grand master of splendid happiness and governor of Deng; soon he was demoted again to registrar of Long prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六月十一日，行及滑州，全忠遣人殺之於白馬驛，投屍於河，時年六十五。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day of the sixth month, as he traveled and reached Hua Prefecture, Quanzhong sent men to kill him at Baima Post Station and cast his corpse into the river; he was then sixty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh day of the sixth month, as he reached Hua prefecture, Quanzhong sent men to kill him at Baima post station and throw his body into the river; he was sixty-five.

sentences.zh: =【贊】=史臣曰：晉卿謹身蒞事，足為純臣，避寇全忠，固彰大節。

translations.literal: =[Appraisal]= The historiographer says: Jinqing was cautious in person and attended to affairs—fully a pure minister; avoiding the bandits he preserved his loyalty, which indeed displayed great integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: The historiographer writes: Jinqing conducted himself with care and served faithfully—he was truly a loyal minister; in fleeing the rebels he preserved his integrity, and that alone shows his great moral stature.

sentences.zh: 然博達精審，豈不知寬猛之道哉！

translations.literal: Yet broadly versed and keenly discriminating—could he not have known the way of lenience and severity!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was learned and discerning—how could he not have known the balance of lenience and severity!

sentences.zh: 奉林甫之旨，順胥吏之意，悅附張倚，欺罔時君。

translations.literal: He followed Linfu's intent, complied with the clerks' wishes, pleased and attached to Zhang Yi, and deceived the sovereign of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Li Linfu's wishes, indulged the clerks, curried favor with Zhang Yi, and deceived his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 生為重臣，諂林甫之勢也；

translations.literal: In life a great minister—this was fawning on Linfu's power;
translations.idiomatic: In life he was a great minister who flattered Li Linfu's power;

sentences.zh: 歿改美謚，引元載之恩焉。

translations.literal: in death his fine posthumous title was changed—this drew on Yuan Zai's grace.
translations.idiomatic: after death his posthumous name was improved through Yuan Zai's favor.

sentences.zh: 或言晉卿不為巧宦者，誠不信也。

translations.literal: Some say Jinqing was not a crafty office-seeker—truly one cannot believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Those who say Jinqing was no crafty courtier simply cannot be believed.

sentences.zh: 冕力贊中興，名居大位，奉公抱義，可以致身；

translations.literal: Mian vigorously aided the restoration, his name occupied the great position, devoted to the public and embracing righteousness—by this one might establish oneself;
translations.idiomatic: Mian vigorously aided the restoration and rose to the highest rank; devoted to the public good and upright in principle, he might have made a name for himself—

sentences.zh: 賣官度僧，是何為政？

translations.literal: yet selling offices and ordaining monks—what kind of government is this?
translations.idiomatic: yet he sold offices and sold ordinations—what sort of government was that?

sentences.zh: 及其老也，貪冒尤深。

translations.literal: When he grew old, his greed and presumption were especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: In old age his greed grew worse still.

sentences.zh: 遵慶學術貞明，為國忠所出；

translations.literal: Zunqing's learning was upright and clear, yet he was sent out by Guozhong;
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing's learning was upright and clear, yet Yang Guozhong posted him out of the capital;

sentences.zh: 恭儉謹密，遇蕭華素知。

translations.literal: respectful, frugal, cautious, and discreet—he met Xiao Hua, who had long known him.
translations.idiomatic: respectful, frugal, and discreet—he won the long-standing regard of Xiao Hua.

sentences.zh: 位重行純，老而彌篤，彼二公固有慚德。

translations.literal: His position was weighty and his conduct pure; in old age he grew ever more steadfast—those two lords indeed had cause for shame beside him.
translations.idiomatic: He held high office with pure conduct and grew more steadfast in old age—the other two men might well have felt shame beside him.

sentences.zh: 向克荷堂構，不墜門風。

translations.literal: Xiang was able to bear the hall's beams and did not let the family's reputation fall.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang upheld the family estate and did not let its reputation fall.

sentences.zh: 樞因盜而振，盜憎而亡，宜哉！

translations.literal: Shu rose through the bandit, the bandit came to hate him and he perished—fitting indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Shu rose through the usurper, and when the usurper turned against him he died—as was fitting!

sentences.zh: 君子守道遠刑，蓋慮此也。

translations.literal: The gentleman keeps the Way and keeps punishment far off—perhaps he takes thought for this.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman holds to the Way and keeps clear of punishment—perhaps he had this in mind.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：奧矣晉卿，貪哉裴冕。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Profound was Jinqing; greedy was Pei Mian.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: Jinqing was profound; Pei Mian was greedy.

sentences.zh: 遵慶父子，及之者鮮。

translations.literal: Zunqing and his son and grandson—few could match them.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing and his line—few could equal them.
